verdicts.earlier_pre_author_item_statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\mu$ a $p$-restricted partition of $d$ and $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ with $\varepsilon_i(\mu)>0$; let $A$ be the good $i$-node and $
u=\mu\setminus A$. For the residue-summand functor $E_i$ of ([[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]]) the module $E_iD(\mu)$ has simple socle and simple head, both isomorphic to $D(
u)$, and the total (ungraded) multiplicity of $D(
u)$ in $E_iD(\mu)$ is $\varepsilon_i(\mu)$. Thus the Loewy endpoints are simple even though the formal character of $E_iD(\mu)$ may contain the additional normal-node factors of ([[thm-normal-node-composition-multiplicities-under-residue-restriction]]).
verdicts.earlier_pre_author_item_strategy: Socle: by ([[cor-socle-of-uncoloured-modular-restriction-is-the-sum-over-good-residues]]) the socle of $\operatorname{Res}D(\mu)$ is $\bigoplus_{j:\varepsilon_j>0}D(\mu\setminus A_j)$, a multiplicity-free sum over distinct simple modules; the $i$-summand $E_iD(\mu)$ contains precisely the summand $D(\mu\setminus A)=D(\nu)$ (the good $i$-node is unique for its residue). Head: the contragredient dual of $E_iD(\mu)$ is $E_i(D(\mu)^*)\cong E_iD(\mu)$ because the primary idempotents are invariant under the antipode ([[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]]) and $D(\mu)$ is self-dual; for a finite-dimensional self-dual module the head is the dual of the socle, so the head is $D(\nu)$ as well ([[def-module-radical-socle-head-and-loewy-series]]). Multiplicity: apply the normal-node theorem ([[thm-normal-node-composition-multiplicities-under-residue-restriction]]) with $A$ the good node; the normal $i$-nodes weakly below $A$ are exactly all normal $i$-nodes, whose number is $\varepsilon_i(\mu)$. The ungraded statement is the one asserted; no graded shift is displayed before the Hecke/KLR bridge. Source: Kleshchev survey Theorem 11.6(ii) with the socle statement of §11.4; the complete proof in the Hecke convention is Brundan 1998 Theorems 5.4 and the §5.5-5.7 transfer, valid at $p=2$.
